what: Second-pass ablation. Every row is 60 CORD-v2 receipts scored by scripts/ocr-eval/score.mjs.
note: results/revamp.json is STALE: the pipeline is deterministic run-to-run (8/8 identical
texts across two runs) but reproduces 0 of 8 of revamp.json's texts, so that file was
written by code that no longer matches the tree. `control` below is the reproduced
control and is what every delta here is measured against.
Parser-only rows are replays over the SAME frozen OCR text, so they are exact A/Bs.
The per-parser-change rows are in-sample (dev); the bundle is confirmed on the holdout.

chain.stage: + next-line amount join (receipt.js)  [= all parser changes]
+ illumination flattening before the paper/table split (binarize.js, preprocess.js)  [SHIPPED]

failureBuckets.method: For each ground-truth item the parser missed, is its name present in the recognised text? That splits an image failure from a parser failure.

whatDidNotWork.physicalImageMeasuresAsPredictors: Correlation of per-receipt strict F1 with illumination non-uniformity (6x6 tile-mean std) r=0.03, tile range r=0.06, Laplacian variance (sharpness) r=0.15, blown highlights r=0.11, crushed blacks r=-0.00, mean luminance r=-0.02. CORD-v2 is photographed well; it cannot be used to credit or refute a shadow/lighting change. That is why synthetic.mjs exists.
whatDidNotWork.summaryLabelGuardWithoutBoundary: Dropping a garbled TOTAL row without also starting the summary block scored 51.3% item F1 / 40.8% strict vs 51.7% / 41.1% with it; the weaker form was discarded.

costs.runtime: Illumination flattening adds one O(pixels) box blur on the ~1000px analysis probe, twice per scan (crop + quad). Mean time 3.14s -> 3.48s on dev (+11%) and 2.70s -> 3.04s on holdout (+13%); MEDIAN time improved on dev (1.97s -> 1.35s) because fewer receipts need the long tail of the candidate race. p90 is worse on the holdout (7.00s -> 10.46s).
costs.zeroItemReceipts: The parser changes alone raised dev zero-item receipts 7 -> 10 (garbled-TOTAL rows were the only thing some receipts produced). Illumination flattening took it back to 5. Across both slices: 22 -> 9.
